title: Higher worker autonomy increased preventative risk-management effort in an online labor experiment
source_unit: 476 U.S.-located online labor-market workers randomly assigned to high- or low-autonomy transcription conditions
geography: United States; online labor market experiment

observations.period: Online labor-market field experiment; NBER Working Paper 30793, 2022 (revised 2026)

denominator.unit: workers who successfully completed the HIT; U.S. location verified

prevention_takeup_high_autonomy.value: 9.7 percentage points higher than low-autonomy condition
prevention_takeup_high_autonomy.unit: take-up of preventative effort to reduce expected total task length

autonomy_condition.value: high-autonomy workers could allocate skipped receipts across two sets; low-autonomy workers had prescribed allocation

observations.method: Randomized online labor-market experiment in which workers transcribed scanned receipts and were assigned different flexibility in allocating skipped tasks; prevention required extra effort but reduced expected task length.
observations.uncertainty: The experiment uses a short online transcription task and a selected U.S.-located worker pool; it does not measure long-run earnings, occupational autonomy, health, household time, bargaining, or actual gig-platform employment. The prevention effect is task-specific and may not generalize to all forms of discretion.
observations.subgroup: U.S.-located online labor-market workers who completed the task; 476 completed the HIT from an initial target of 500.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher autonomy may reduce the effective cost of prevention by allowing workers to redistribute effort rather than increase intrinsic motivation; greater discretion can therefore change risk management without improving overall work conditions.

boundary: This record adds a causal task-autonomy-to-risk-management route: high autonomy increased preventative effort in a short online labor task. It does not establish durable worker control, earnings, household security, bargaining power, health, or broad gig-work effects.
